record.context_brief: How small finite-group symmetry numbers can be
record.original_question: Given ε > 0 and an integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G whose maximal symmetry number ms_r(G) is smaller than ε?

evidence.quote: Surprisingly, but for non-commutative groups of even order the inequality msr(G) ≥ 1/r2 does not hold anymore: it was noticed in [6] that msr(Q8) = 1/8 < 1/22, where Q8 = {±1, ±i, ±j, ±k} is the group of quaternions.
Question 7.8 ([6]). Does for every ε > 0 and r > 1 there exist a finite group G with msr(G) < ε?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group. A subset S ⊆ G is called symmetric if there exists an element c ∈ G (the "center" of symmetry) such that S = cS⁻¹c, i.e., x ∈ S if and only if cx⁻¹c ∈ S. For an integer r ≥ 2 and an r-coloring χ : G → {1, …, r}, let MS(G, χ) denote the largest cardinality of a monochromatic symmetric subset of G under χ. Define the maximal symmetry number

  ms_r(G) := (1/|G|) · min_χ MS(G, χ),

where the minimum is taken over all r-colorings χ : G → {1, …, r}.

Question: Is it true that for every ε > 0 and every integer r > 1 there exists a finite group G with ms_r(G) < ε?

(Background fact: for the quaternion group Q₈ = {±1, ±i, ±j, ±k} one has ms₂(Q₈) = 1/8 < 1/r² with r = 2, so the lower bound ms_r(G) ≥ 1/r² that holds for finite abelian groups fails for general finite groups.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2011 survey by Banakh and collaborators on symmetry and colorings. A targeted web search did not surface any later paper claiming a resolution (positive or negative) for arbitrary r > 1 and ε > 0. The status therefore appears to remain unresolved as of the search, though no definitive recent survey was located.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry and colorings: some results and open problems, II
status_evidence.snippet: We survey some principal results and open problems related to colorings of geometric and algebraic objects endowed with symmetries, concentrating the exposition on the maximal symmetry numbers of such objects.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open question in a survey on maximal symmetry numbers.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry (Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets)
status_evidence.snippet: Definitions of ms(Ω,r) for spaces endowed with symmetry, including finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Background framework for ms_r(G) defined in earlier work by the same group of authors.
